calibration_corrections.original: critical_mode = min(raw scores) over mixed-direction, mixed-unit metrics
calibration_corrections.corrected: all modes return time-to-threshold in years; min time = occurs first; direction unambiguous
calibration_corrections.effect: foundation_settlement no longer incorrectly dominates regimes with low groundwater

calibration_corrections.summary: lateral ties miscounted as load-path redundancy
calibration_corrections.original: lateral ties incremented R0 (min-cut), giving identical R0 across all archetypes
calibration_corrections.corrected: graph theory (Menger): intra-layer ties cannot cross any source→sink cut; R0 = independent foundation columns only; ties → load_sharing_factor that slows cascade without adding paths
calibration_corrections.effect: R0 now distinct across all archetypes: granite=2, roman_pozzolan=3, dry_stone=4, bamboo=8, etc.

calibration_corrections.summary: longevity yardstick too narrow for renewal architecture
calibration_corrections.original: all archetypes ranked by survival fraction to a shared horizon
calibration_corrections.corrected: design-intent axis added; renewal archetypes scored on cadence fitness + substrate-debt flux; permanent archetypes retain longevity fitness; judging a sod house by a granite yardstick is a metrology-scope error
calibration_corrections.effect: ice/snow/sod/bamboo score highest on renewal lens; massive_arch/concrete/modern_reinforced score highest accumulated substrate debt

claims.claim: Roman pozzolan achieves the highest survival fraction in freeze_thaw environments
claims.mechanism: Porosity 10.5% keeps ice-lens saturation below Fagerlund critical threshold; tobermorite matrix impedes crack propagation; C-A-S-H gel fills micro-cracks on re-wetting
claims.falsifier: Any other archetype achieves higher survival_frac at n≥2000, horizon=500yr in freeze_thaw regime
claims.reference: Jackson et al. 2017 (Baianus Sinus cores): porosity 10.0–11.0%; Pantheon dome intact after 2000yr including frost seasons

claims.claim: Roman pozzolan achieves the highest survival fraction in coastal_salt environments
claims.mechanism: Tobermorite self-heals hairline cracks in seawater contact; no rebar means no chloride depassivation pathway; Friedel's salt binds Cl⁻ ions; granite loses to haloclasty (salt-crystal growth in micro-pores reduces effective FT budget)
claims.falsifier: Any other archetype achieves higher survival_frac at n≥2000, horizon=500yr in coastal_salt regime
claims.reference: Caesarea Maritima breakwater intact after 2000yr; Portus Cosanus seawall cores show tobermorite growth in seawater voids

claims.claim: Dry stone achieves the highest survival fraction and longest median collapse time in wet_clay environments
claims.mechanism: Open joints drain pore pressure freely (drainage=0.95 → 80% reduction in effective settlement rate); individual stones accommodate differential movement without propagating a through-crack; span_m=650 encodes very large settlement tolerance; freeze_thaw dominates over settlement for dry_stone
claims.falsifier: Any other archetype achieves higher survival_frac or longer median_collapse at n≥2000 in wet_clay regime
claims.reference: Scottish clearance dykes on clay soils: many still standing 200–400yr; Norse longhouse dry-stone plinths in wet peat soils surviving 500+yr

claims.claim: Roman pozzolan achieves near-zero survival in seismic environments
claims.mechanism: Rigidity=0.88, E≈20–25 GPa, no ductility: elastic energy releases catastrophically at joint_shear under high ground-motion; zero seismic design load provides no ductile reserve; 3.6% survival reflects rare low-seismic draws from the environment distribution
claims.falsifier: roman_pozzolan survival_frac > 5% at n≥2000, horizon=500yr in seismic regime
claims.reference: 426 CE Kourion Cyprus earthquake destroyed all local Roman concrete structures; Lisbon 1755 — Roman concrete ruins collapsed

claims.claim: Dry stone achieves approximately 91% survival in temperate_stable environments
claims.mechanism: R0=4 independent load paths; lateral_ties=6 header courses slow load-concentration cascade; open drainage prevents frost saturation; creep_rate=2e-7 (near-zero); seismic_factor=0 (rocking decouples)
claims.falsifier: dry_stone survival_frac outside [85%, 95%] at n≥2000, horizon=500yr in temperate_stable regime
claims.reference: English Heritage 2004 survey of Cotswold dry-stone walls: ~91% of pre-1800 walls still load-bearing

claims.claim: The lowest-debt renewal archetypes (ice, snow, sod, bamboo, straw, cob) achieve lower substrate_debt_flux than any permanent archetype in temperate_stable conditions
claims.mechanism: return_to_substrate ≥ 0.95 for this group; their (1−return)/actual_life values are < 0.00100/yr. Even the best permanents (granite, roman_pozzolan) achieve 0.001–0.002/yr because quarried/cast mass stays locked. Boundary cases (timber_laced ≈ field_stone) can overlap — the claim applies to the top renewal tier only.
claims.falsifier: Any of ice/snow/sod/bamboo/straw/cob achieves higher substrate_debt_flux than granite in temperate_stable conditions

claims.claim: Ice and snow accumulate zero net substrate debt over any time horizon
claims.mechanism: return_to_substrate = 1.0 for both; substrate_debt_flux = (1 − 1.0) / life = 0 exactly; water cycle returns all mass to atmosphere and precipitation
claims.falsifier: substrate_debt_flux ≠ 0 for ice or snow (would indicate a data-entry error in _PHILOSOPHY)

claims.claim: Massive_arch and concrete-family permanents have the highest substrate_debt_flux among all archetypes in temperate_stable conditions
claims.mechanism: These archetypes combine near-zero return_to_substrate (0.05) with moderate actual life (250–330yr in temperate_stable) → (1−0.05)/~300yr ≈ 0.003–0.004/yr. This exceeds granite (0.002/yr, long life amortises the extraction cost) and all renewal archetypes except treehouse.
claims.falsifier: Any renewal-intent archetype or granite achieves higher substrate_debt_flux than massive_arch in temperate_stable conditions
